mainTopic: Rejecting רב יוסף's ברייתא, a יבם's promise to share the estate, and the משנה's rules about a יבמה after יבום
overview: The amud opens by defending the ברייתא of רב יוסף: maybe it follows רבי נתן, who holds that a debtor can be made to pay his creditor's creditor directly. Then the גמרא gives the real reason to reject it. It would need two stringencies about כתובה, one from רבי מאיר and one from רבי נתן, and no תנא holds both. רבא realizes this is what אביי meant by 'this is not a משנה.' Next comes a story: a man offers to split his dead brother's property with his brother, even 'from now,' so the brother won't disqualify their יבמה with a גט. מר בר רב אשי explains that this cannot work, because before יבום the property is not his to give. Along the way the גמרא reconciles two reports of רבי יוחנן about acquiring a cow after thirty days: it depends on whether the owner said 'acquire from now.' The הלכה is that dividing the property does nothing, whether before or after יבום. The גמרא then returns to the משנה: ריש לקיש rereads the attached produce as 'hers,' and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains that after יבום she is a regular wife, divorced with a גט alone. The amud ends by asking why the משנה needs to teach that he may remarry her.

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא follows רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the claim that the ברייתא is unreliable, suggesting it could follow רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it is the opinion of רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is defending the ברייתא that was just called unreliable. It suggests that the ברייתא could fit the view of רבי נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the ברייתא looked like it could not match any known opinion. If רבי נתן's rule (paying a creditor's creditor directly) explains it, then the ברייתא is not mistaken after all.

keyTerms.meaning: maybe, perhaps

phrases.english: Perhaps it is the opinion of Rabbi Natan.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ברייתא of רב יוסף that was just called unreliable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the earlier claim (before this section) that the ברייתא is unreliable.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the earlier claim that the ברייתא matches no known opinion.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The earlier claim did not consider רבי נתן's rule about collecting from a creditor's debtor.

steps.title: רבי נתן's rule: pay the creditor's creditor directly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי נתן's ברייתא: if A owes B and B owes C, the court takes the money from A and gives it straight to C.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי נתן says, from where do we know that if one man is owed a מנה by his friend, and that friend is owed by another, the court takes from this one and gives to that one? The verse says: 'And he shall give it to the one to whom he is guilty.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי נתן's rule to back up the suggestion in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן learns from the פסוק that money owed to a debtor is tied up for that debtor's own creditor. This is the idea later called שעבודא דרבי נתן. So in our case, money owed to the dead man can be collected for his wife's כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: creditor, someone owed money
a sum of 100 זוז
take from this one and give to that one
the verse teaches
he is guilty (owes) to him

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for שעבודא דרבי נתן, a basic rule about debts that comes up across ש״ס.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Natan says:
From where do we know, regarding one who is owed a maneh by his fellow,
and his fellow is owed by another fellow,
from where do we know that we take from this one and give to that one?
phrases.notes: Take from the last borrower and give straight to the first lender, skipping the middle man.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And he shall give it to the one to whom he is guilty."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the suggestion in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא could follow רבי נתן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי נתן's ברייתא learning from 'ונתן לאשר אשם לו' that a debtor pays his creditor's creditor.

steps.title: No תנא holds both stringencies about כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a better reason to reject the ברייתא: it needs both רבי מאיר's and רבי נתן's stringencies, and no one holds both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: we have not found a תנא who is strict with two stringencies about כתובה. It is either like רבי מאיר or like רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the old reason and gives a new, stronger reason why the ברייתא cannot be trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To explain the ברייתא you need two strict rules. One is רבי מאיר's, that movable property is tied to the כתובה. The other is רבי נתן's, that debts owed to the husband are tied to the כתובה. Each תנא holds only one of them, so a ברייתא that needs both matches no one.

keyTerms.meaning: we have not found
a sage of the משנה period
two stringencies
the marriage contract and the money it promises the wife

steps.confusionAlert: רבי נתן's view is not being rejected. The point is only that nobody holds רבי נתן's view and רבי מאיר's view together.

phrases.english: Rather: we have not found a tanna
who is strict with two stringencies regarding a ketubah,
rather, either like Rabbi Meir
or like Rabbi Natan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לָא אַשְׁכְּחַן תַּנָּא דְּמַחְמִיר תְּרֵי חוּמְרֵי בִּכְתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that רבי נתן explains one part, but shows the ברייתא still needs a second stringency.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא quoted by רב יוסף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא needs both רבי מאיר's and רבי נתן's stringencies, but no תנא holds both, so it matches no one.

steps.title: רבא finally understands אביי
steps.stepSummary: רבא says this explains אביי's comment 'this is not a משנה,' which he had not understood before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If so, this is what I heard from אביי, who said 'This is not a משנה,' and I did not know what it meant.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא closes the discussion. The reason in step 3 is what אביי meant when he rejected this teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי had dismissed the ברייתא without saying why, and רבא had not understood. Now רבא sees that the 'two stringencies' problem is the reason, which confirms that the ברייתא is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
this is (what was meant)
this is not a reliable teaching

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is rejected because it needs both רבי מאיר's and רבי נתן's stringencies about כתובה, and no תנא holds both. That is what אביי meant by 'this is not a משנה.'

phrases.english: Rava said: If so,
this is what I heard from Abaye,
who said: "This is not a mishnah,"
phrases.notes: Here 'משנה' means any authoritative teaching, and this one is the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and I did not know what it meant.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִם כֵּן, הַיְינוּ דִּשְׁמַעְנָא לֵיהּ לְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms that step 3 is the right reason for rejecting the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא is not authoritative, because it combines two stringencies that no single תנא holds.

steps.title: A brother wants to disqualify the יבמה with a גט
steps.stepSummary: A new story: a man in מתא מחסיא has a יבמה waiting for him, and his brother wants to disqualify her by giving her a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man whose יבמה fell before him in מתא מחסיא. His brother wanted to disqualify her from him with a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story, similar to the earlier story about the man from פומבדיתא. This step sets the scene for the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One brother is in line to do יבום. The other brother wants to give the widow a גט so that she becomes forbidden to him. The next steps show that the reason is the dead brother's property.

keyTerms.meaning: a widow who needs יבום or חליצה
fell before him (became his to do יבום with)
to disqualify her with a גט

phrases.english: There was a certain man to whom a yevamah fell
in Mata Meḥasya.
His brother wanted to disqualify her
from him by means of a bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דִּנְפַלָה לֵיהּ יְבָמָה בְּמָתָא מַחְסֵיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story, separate from the discussion about the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a brother wants to disqualify the יבמה with a גט.

steps.title: The man offers to share the property
steps.stepSummary: The man asks his brother why he is doing this, and offers to split the property if that is the worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is your thinking? If it is because of the property, I will divide the property with you.
steps.whatsHappening: The man asks his brother what he is worried about. He also tries to solve the problem right away by offering to split the estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brother who does יבום would inherit the dead brother's property. The man guesses that this is why his brother is upset, so he promises to share it.

keyTerms.meaning: what is your thinking?
property
I will divide with you

phrases.english: He said to him: What is your thinking?
If it is because of the property,
phrases.notes: He means the dead brother's estate.

phrases.english: I will divide the property with you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The man answers his brother's plan to disqualify the יבמה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the brother wants to disqualify the יבמה. The man suggests the property is the reason.

steps.title: The brother fears a trick like the one in פומבדיתא
steps.stepSummary: The brother says he is afraid the man will break his promise, like the swindler from פומבדיתא did.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am afraid you will do to me what the swindler from פומבדיתא did.
steps.whatsHappening: The brother explains why the promise is not enough for him: he is afraid it will not be kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier story, a man from פומבדיתא promised to share an inheritance and then went back on his word. The brother fears the same thing here, so a promise about the future does not reassure him.

keyTerms.meaning: I am afraid
a man from פומבדיתא
swindler, cheat

phrases.english: He said to him: I am afraid
that you will do to me
as the swindler from Pumbedita did.
phrases.notes: This is the earlier story, where a man promised to share the inheritance and then went back on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִסְתְּפֵינָא דְּעָבְדַתְּ לִי כְּדַעֲבַיד פּוּמְבְּדִיתָאָה רַמָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the man's question, and explains why his offer is not enough.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The brother is afraid the promise to share will not be kept, like what happened in פומבדיתא.

steps.title: The man offers to divide the property now
steps.stepSummary: To calm his brother's fear, the man offers to have the property divided starting right now.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If you want, divide it for yourself from now.
steps.whatsHappening: The man answers his brother's fear by offering to make the division take effect right away, instead of only promising it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A promise for later can be broken, but a deal made now cannot be taken back. By offering to divide 'from now,' the man tries to remove the worry about being cheated.

keyTerms.meaning: if you want
from now

phrases.english: He said to him: If you want,
divide it for yourself from now.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי בָּעֵית — פְּלוֹג לָךְ מֵהַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the brother's fear from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical fix: turning a promise for later into a division made now.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A promise to share the property could be broken, like in פומבדיתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The man proposes that the division take effect from now, so the brother will not need to worry about being cheated. Step 10 shows that this does not actually work.

steps.title: The cow that is acquired after thirty days
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי brings רבי יוחנן's ruling that pulling a cow now can make it acquired thirty days later. This looks like it could support dividing the property 'from now.'
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: Even though רב דימי reported in the name of רבי יוחנן that if someone says, 'Go pull this cow, but it will only be yours after thirty days,' the buyer acquires it after thirty days, even if by then the cow is standing in a meadow.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי opens with 'even though' and quotes a case that seems to support the man's offer to divide 'from now.' This is a setup: in the next line he will explain why that case does not apply here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוחנן's case, the act of acquiring (pulling the cow) happens now, but ownership only takes effect thirty days later. It works even if the cow is in a place where it could not be acquired at that later time. That suggests a קנין done now can take effect later, which might seem to help the יבם's offer.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling: a way of acquiring an animal or movable item by drawing it toward oneself
Cow
Acquired, owned
Meadow or marsh: an open place that does not belong to the buyer
When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל): a formula for reporting teachings from there

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי,
phrases.english: Even though when Rav Dimi came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who says to his fellow:
"Go and pull this cow,
and it will not be acquired by you
until after thirty days,"
after thirty days he has acquired it,
and even if it is standing in a meadow.
phrases.notes: The meadow isn't the buyer's land, so he couldn't acquire the cow there on day thirty. The pulling done back on day one is what counts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the man's offer in step 8 to divide the property 'from now' by bringing a case that seems to support it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קנין done now can make an item acquired after a delay, even if the item is later in a place where it could not be acquired.

steps.title: The cow was his to give, the property is not
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי says the cow case is different. The seller already owned the cow, but the יבם does not yet own his dead brother's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is in his power. Here, it is not in his power.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי finishes his point and explains why the cow case does not help the יבם's offer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner of the cow could transfer it right away, so he can also choose to delay the transfer. The יבם has not done יבום yet, so the dead brother's property is not his. He cannot give away 'from now' what he does not own now, so his offer is worthless.

keyTerms.meaning: In his hand, in his power: he owns it and can transfer it
Not in his power: he does not own it yet
There / here: words used to contrast two cases

steps.whatToRemember: Delaying a קנין only works when the giver owns the item at the moment of the קנין. A יבם before יבום cannot divide property that is not yet his.

phrases.english: There, it is in his power;
phrases.notes: "There" is the cow case. The seller owns the cow right now.

phrases.english: here, it is not in his power.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes מר בר רב אשי's statement by rejecting the comparison he raised in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the cow case to support the יבם's 'from now' division.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cow's owner owns it at the time of the קנין. The יבם does not yet own the property.

steps.title: Another report: רבי יוחנן said he does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבין reported the opposite ruling from רבי יוחנן about the cow.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: he does not acquire!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the cow ruling itself, because a different report of רבי יוחנן says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי reported that the buyer acquires the cow after thirty days. רבין reported that he does not. Both cannot be right as stated, so the גמרא needs to explain how they fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely: opens a challenge from a source
He does not acquire

phrases.english: But when Ravin came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said: He does not acquire!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the cow ruling quoted in step 9 with a second report that contradicts it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's report of רבי יוחנן's ruling about the cow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two reports of the same רבי יוחנן give opposite rulings about the same case.

steps.title: It depends on saying 'acquire from now'
steps.stepSummary: The two reports describe different cases. If the owner said 'acquire from now,' the buyer acquires after thirty days. If not, he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ruling is where he told him 'acquire from now.' That ruling is where he did not tell him 'acquire from now.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each report is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the owner says 'acquire from now,' the קנין is done now, and the thirty-day wait only delays when it takes final effect. Without those words, the whole acquisition is pushed off to day thirty. By then the act of pulling is long over, so nothing happens.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: introduces an answer to a contradiction
Acquire from now: the קנין starts working at this moment
This one ... that one: splits two sources into two different cases

steps.whatToRemember: A delayed acquisition through pulling works only if the owner said 'acquire from now.'

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where he said to him "Acquire from now,"
that is where he did not say to him "Acquire from now."

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ קְנֵי מֵעַכְשָׁיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each report refers to a different wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two reports of רבי יוחנן seemed to disagree about the very same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: He acquires if the owner said 'acquire from now.' He does not acquire if the owner did not say it.

steps.title: Dividing the property after יבום
steps.stepSummary: עולא is asked whether the division counts if the יבם first does יבום and then divides the property with his brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked עולא: If he did יבום and afterward divided the property, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the story and asks עולא whether the promised division works at all. The first case is a division made after יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After יבום the property belongs to the יבם, so the problem from step 10 (he does not own it) is gone. The question is whether a division done at that point is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked him: introduces a question put to a sage
He did יבום, married his dead brother's wife
He divided the property
What is the law?

phrases.english: They asked Ulla:
If he did yibum and afterward divided, what is the law?
phrases.notes: "Divided" means he shared the property with his brother, as he promised in step 6.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about the cow and returns to the יבם's promise to divide.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a division of the property made after יבום valid?

steps.title: עולא: the division after יבום does nothing
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that a division made after יבום has no effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: He has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא rules that even when the יבם divides after יבום, the division does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising, because after יבום he does own the property. The גמרא has not yet given a reason here. It just states that the division is empty.

keyTerms.meaning: He has done nothing at all: the act has no legal effect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the reason is that he does not own the property. That was the problem before יבום (step 10). Here he already did יבום, and עולא still says it does nothing.

phrases.english: He has done nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A division made after יבום has no effect.

steps.title: Dividing the property before יבום
steps.stepSummary: עולא is asked about the reverse order: the יבם divides first and does יבום afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he divided and afterward did יבום, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא is asked a second question that flips the order: division first, then יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the division happens before the יבם owns the property, just like the 'from now' offer. The question is whether the יבום that comes later makes the earlier division take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: And afterward

phrases.english: If he divided and afterward did yibum, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the opposite order from the case in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a division made before יבום valid once he later does יבום?

steps.title: עולא: the division before יבום also does nothing
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that a division made before יבום also has no effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: He has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives the same answer as before: dividing before יבום does not count either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits מר בר רב אשי's point in step 10: before יבום the property is not his to divide. So in both orders, the division has no legal force.
steps.whatToRemember: According to עולא, the יבם's division of the property with his brother has no effect, whether it comes before or after יבום.

phrases.english: He has done nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A division made before יבום has no effect, even after he later does יבום.

steps.title: רב ששת: Why Ask the Second Question at All?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת argues that once dividing after יבום has no effect, dividing before יבום surely has no effect, so the second question was pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objects: If he did יבום and then divided, and it means nothing, then if he divided and only afterward did יבום, is there even a question?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת challenges the way the questions to עולא were reported. He says the second question should never have been asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After יבום the יבם is the strongest he will ever be over the property, and even then his division does nothing. So before יבום, when he is weaker, his division obviously does nothing too. Asking about the weaker case after the stronger one was already answered makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges it; a strong objection
Now (opens a 'how much more so' argument)
Is it even a question? (it is obvious)
He divided (the property)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet objects to it:
Now if he did levirate marriage and afterward divided,
he has done nothing at all,
then if he divided and afterward did levirate marriage, is there a question?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the second question (Step 15) given the answer to the first (Step 14).
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that עולא was asked both questions, one after the other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A 'how much more so' argument: if the stronger case does nothing, the weaker case obviously does nothing, so asking about it is pointless.

steps.title: Two Separate Incidents
steps.stepSummary: The two questions were asked on two different occasions, so each one got its own answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were two separate incidents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב ששת. The two questions were not asked together, so the second was not a pointless follow-up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's challenge only works if one person asked both questions in a row. If two real cases came before עולא at different times, each needed its own ruling, even if one ruling could have been worked out from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: There were two incidents
An actual case that happened

phrases.english: There were two incidents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's challenge in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the report: two separate events instead of one question and a follow-up
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both questions were asked together, so the second one was unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each question came from a separate real case, so each needed its own answer.

steps.title: רבין's Report: No Effect in Either Order
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that ריש לקיש said dividing the property means nothing, whether it happens before or after יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said that ריש לקיש said: Whether he did יבום and then divided, or divided and then did יבום, he has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another report from ארץ ישראל. It states the rule as one statement covering both orders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is no question and answer, just one clear rule from ריש לקיש. He gives the same result as עולא: in both orders, the division has no effect.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Whether... or... (both cases are the same)
He has done nothing at all; the act has no effect

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said that Reish Lakish said:
Whether he did levirate marriage and afterward divided,
or he divided and afterward did levirate marriage —
he has done nothing at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second report of the same ruling, stated as one rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dividing the property has no effect, whether it is done before or after יבום.

steps.title: The הלכה: The Division Has No Effect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the division has no effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: he has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling for this whole discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every report agrees that the division does nothing, in either order. The גמרא makes that the practical הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: And the practical הלכה is

steps.whatToRemember: A יבם who divides the property, before or after יבום, has done nothing, and this is the הלכה.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: he has done nothing at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes Step 19 the practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The division has no effect in either order.

steps.title: How Can the Attached Produce Be His?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in the משנה, who say produce attached to the ground belongs to the יבם. It asks how that can be, since all the property is a guarantee for her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: The חכמים say produce attached to the ground is his. Why? All of his property is a guarantee for her כתובה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים give the attached produce to the יבם. But the dead husband's property is all tied up as security for the woman's כתובה. So how can he take the produce for himself?

keyTerms.meaning: Produce still attached to the ground
Why?
A guarantee and security (for a debt)
The marriage contract money owed to the wife

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
Produce attached to the ground is his.
Why?
But all of his property
is a guarantee and security for her marriage contract!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? וְהָא כׇּל נְכָסָיו אַחְרָאִין וְעַרְבָאִין לִכְתוּבָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's ruling that attached produce belongs to the יבם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All the property is security for her כתובה, so he should not be able to take the produce for himself.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: Read It as 'Hers'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש changes the wording of the משנה. The attached produce is hers, not his.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Teach it as 'hers.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the challenge by changing the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the new wording, the חכמים say the produce is the woman's. That fits the rule that all the property backs up her כתובה, so the problem goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Hers

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not explaining the word 'his' in a new way. He is replacing it with 'hers.'

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Teach: it is hers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says the produce is his, which clashes with her כתובה rights.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה should read 'hers,' which fits the rule that the property secures her כתובה.

steps.title: What Does 'Like His Wife' Teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that once he marries her she is like his wife, and asks what הלכה that line comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: Once he married her, she is like his wife. For what הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and asks what practical rule it is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After יבום she obviously becomes his wife, so the line seems to add nothing new. The גמרא wants to know what specific rule the משנה means by it.

keyTerms.meaning: He took her in marriage (did יבום)
She is like his (regular) wife
For what הלכה? What does it teach?

phrases.english: If he married her, she is like his wife.
For what halacha?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical rule the משנה teaches by calling her 'like his wife.'

steps.title: He Divorces Her With a גט and May Remarry Her
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains that she is like his wife in two ways. He divorces her with a גט, and he may take her back afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: It teaches that he divorces her with a גט and may remarry her.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא answers the question by giving two rules that follow from her being 'like his wife.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: After יבום she is treated as a regular wife. So the marriage ends with a גט, and after the divorce he is allowed to marry her again, just like any man and his divorced wife.

keyTerms.meaning: A bill of divorce
He divorces her
He takes her back (remarries her)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
To say that he divorces her with a bill of divorce
and may take her back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is like his wife in that he divorces her with a גט and may remarry her afterward.

steps.title: Divorce With a גט Is Obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first half of the answer. Of course he divorces her with a גט, so why would the משנה need to teach that?
steps.simpleTranslation: He divorces her with a גט? That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on part of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's answer. This sets up an explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she is his wife through יבום, a גט seems like the only normal way to end the marriage. So it looks like the משנה would not need to say it, and the גמרא asks why it does.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious

phrases.english: He divorces her with a bill of divorce? That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first half of the answer in Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה teaches he divorces her with a גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wife is always divorced with a גט, so this seems too obvious for the משנה to need to teach.

steps.title: Without the משנה we might think she needs חליצה too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the משנה must teach that a גט is enough. We might have thought the original יבום tie still clings to her, so she could only leave through חליצה. The משנה teaches that a גט alone works.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: the Torah said "and he shall do יבום with her," and the first יבום tie is still on her. So a גט should not be enough for her, and she should need חליצה. The משנה teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 25 by showing what mistake we could have made without the משנה's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her marriage to the יבם came through the מצוה of יבום, so we might think a trace of that יבום bond stays on her. Because of that, we could think only חליצה can fully release her. The משנה tells us that once he married her she is a regular wife, and a regular wife leaves with a גט alone.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said: introduces the wrong idea we would have had
"And he shall do יבום with her": the Torah's word for the levirate marriage
The Merciful One: the Torah
The ceremony that releases a widow from the יבם without marriage
It teaches us: shows the משנה is teaching something new

phrases.english: You might have said:
The Merciful One said: "and he shall do יבום with her,"
and the first יבום tie is still on her.
So a גט should not be enough for her,
but only with חליצה.
So the משנה teaches us that a גט is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25 by showing the mistake the משנה's teaching prevents.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows a possible mistaken assumption that makes the teaching needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the old יבום tie is still on her, a גט would not be enough and she would need חליצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the יבם married her she is a full wife, and a גט alone releases her.

steps.title: Why teach that he may take her back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now turns to the second half of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's explanation. It asks why the משנה would need to teach that he may take her back after divorcing her, since that seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He may take her back": that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second half of the answer from step 24, just as it did with the first half. This sets up an explanation for why this point needs teaching too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any man who divorces his wife may remarry her, so it seems there is nothing new here. The challenge has the same shape as step 25. Now the גמרא needs to find some mistaken idea that would make this teaching necessary.

keyTerms.meaning: He takes her back: remarries her after the divorce
It is obvious: a challenge that something did not need to be taught

phrases.english: "He may take her back": that is obvious!
phrases.notes: This quotes the second half of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's answer from step 24.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the גט half, the גמרא turns to challenge the second half of the step 24 answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement that the יבם may take her back after divorcing her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Any divorced wife may be remarried by her husband, so the משנה would seem to teach nothing new.
